description: 15 of the 21 partitions inventory.md establishes (P7 Worker lifecycle through P21 Sergeant-authored operational skills) are still recorded as `pending` in partition-ledger.md, this far into the run (past 30-normalize, 40-classify, 50-synthesize, 60-draft, and 70-lint, all of which completed their ordinary work on the corpus as it stood). This covers 54 of the 82 decompose files inventory.md scoped in (66% of the corpus by file count): all of bin/sgt-interactive-worker, sgt-validate, sgt-validation-worker, _sgt-harness.sh, _sgt-intent.sh, sgt-td-memory (P7); sgt-respond, sgt-ack-response, sgt-wake, sgt-recover, _sgt-response-lock.sh (P8); sgt-drain, sgt-drain-force, sgt-undrain, _sgt-drain.sh (P9); sgt-watch, sgt-cleanup (P10); sgt-callback, sgt-notify, sgt-review-findings, sgt-no-mistakes-finding (P11); the wiki skill and wiki-daily-digest (P12); sgt-dag-run, sgt-dag-dispatch-hook (P13); _sgt-lib.sh, _sgt-bash-version.sh (P14); and all 21 files of the vendored/authored skill trees (P15-P21). 00-contract/output/contract.md §5 states this run is 'bounded by, and done when, each stage's own CONTEXT.md-declared durable outcome has been reached in sequence' — 20-harvest's own declared outcome (per partition-ledger.md's header, seeded from all 21 of inventory.md's partitions) was not reached, yet every later stage proceeded as ordinary work rather than treating the corpus as incomplete.
evidence: partition-ledger.md rows P7-P21 all show `Status: pending` with blank `Unit id range`/`Notes` cells; inventory.md 'Totals' table states 82 decompose files across 21 partitions (§§39-64); 00-contract/output/contract.md §5 'Success criteria'.

description: consequence-class-sweep.md contains exactly 28 data rows, one per file — covering only the 28 decompose files in partitions P1-P6. The other 54 decompose files inventory.md names (partitions P7-P21) have no row at all, not even a row with 'swept, none found' cells. This is not a blank-cell gap (which the sweep's own header says is never left) — it is an entirely missing row for two-thirds of the files the sweep was scoped to cover.
evidence: Recounted consequence-class-sweep.md's data rows directly: 28 (AGENTS.md through templates/worker-brief.md, i.e. exactly the P1-P6 file list). inventory.md §'Totals' states 82 decompose files total; the sweep's own header requires one row per decompose file named in inventory.md.

description: Recomputed the distinct `source.path` count directly over ../20-harvest/output/behavior-units.ndjson myself (not copied from any artifact): 28 distinct files, not the 82 decompose files inventory.md scopes in. 30-normalize (312 records), 40-classify (312 records), 50-synthesize ('Clusters ... (312 records)', 'the full 312-record ledger'), and 60-draft ('18/18 candidates', 'against the full 312-record ledger') all treat 312 as if it were the complete corpus — none of these four downstream artifacts states, anywhere I could find, that the corpus underlying them covers only 6 of 21 partitions / 28 of 82 files. The 18 materialized draft workflow packages under .sergeant/drafts/workflows/ are consequently a decomposition of roughly one-third of the subject repository's decompose-dispositioned files, not the repository as a whole — entire subsystems (worker recovery internals beyond what P1-P6 touched tangentially, drain control, fleet cleanup/watch mechanics, callback/escalation routing, wiki capture, DAG dispatch, the shared bash foundation, and all 21 vendored/authored skill files) never had a chance to produce a behavior unit, a classification, a candidate, or a draft package.
evidence: python recount: `len({json.loads(l)['source']['path'] for l in open('20-harvest/output/behavior-units.ndjson')})` = 28. `wc -l` on behavior-units.ndjson / behavior-units.normalized.ndjson / classifications.ndjson each = 312. 50-synthesize/output/candidates.md line 3, line 8-16 ('312 records', 'the 312 classification records'); 60-draft/output/draft-report.md line 12 ('18 workflow candidates from ... Buckets 1-3') and line 273 ('the full 312-record ledger'). Same root cause as AF-0001/AF-0002; recorded separately because this is the corpus-count self-consistency check the checklist names independently.

description: All five stage-context records classified under workflow=worker-response-and-recovery, stage=recover-worker justify their §6.3 'no' answer by asserting the checkpoint 'is established more specifically elsewhere' or 'already established at BU-0039/BU-0146[/BU-0159]' — but no representation:stage record for recover-worker exists anywhere in the 312-record corpus (independently confirmed: grepping classifications.ndjson for `"stage": "recover-worker"` combined with `"representation": "stage"` returns zero matches). Each record's demotion below stage rests on a sibling stage-context record's own claim that the real checkpoint exists, and that chain never terminates in an actual stage record — it is circular, not merely unattached. 50-synthesize/output/candidates.md's own 'Unattached records' section (carried into 60-draft/output/draft-report.md) already discloses the aggregate fact that no stage record exists for recover-worker and singles this case out as 'the single sharpest instance', but neither artifact notes that the classify-stage's own rationale text is what manufactures the false impression a stage checkpoint exists. Independently re-applying §6.3 to the five records' combined content (gating on prior reconciliation/generation/pane-identity evidence; one-shot-per-attempt with durable recording; escalation on three named failure conditions; diagnose-and-preserve-state before any kill/relaunch; naming the one supported recovery path) reads as exactly the entry/exit/measurable checkpoint §6.3 asks about, in a workflow whose own name is 'worker-response-and-recovery' — the more honest reading is that this cluster should have produced a stage record, not that a stage record exists 'elsewhere'.
evidence: classifications.ndjson rationale fields for BU-0039 ('...feeding the recovery checkpoint that's established more specifically elsewhere'), BU-0146 ('...restating BU-0039 more specifically'), BU-0159 ('...already established at BU-0039/BU-0146'), BU-0174 ('...already established at BU-0039/BU-0146/BU-0159'), BU-0286 ('...applied to the already-established recovery/status checkpoints (BU-0146/BU-0283)'); grep for representation:stage + stage:recover-worker in classifications.ndjson: no matches; 50-synthesize/output/candidates.md 'Unattached records' section (worker-response-and-recovery | recover-worker row, and the prose naming it 'the single sharpest case').

description: Bucket 6 (obsolete-mechanism) is reported empty with only a count-based justification ('Zero classification records ... carry an obsolete-mechanism disposition ... checked directly against the full 312-record ledger') — this shows the classify output was zero, not that anyone tried routing real candidate units to the obsolete-mechanism question and found they genuinely didn't fit, which is what the Unused-tiers check (challenge-checklist.md Axis 4 §3) requires before accepting a zero-count tier as clean. No candidate units are named, and no per-unit 'why it does not clear this rung' reasoning is given, unlike the reimplementation-test reasoning given elsewhere in this same document for other rungs. (shared-context and engine-gap are both non-zero in this corpus, so obsolete-mechanism is the only rung this check actually applies to.)
evidence: 50-synthesize/output/candidates.md lines 938-944 ('## Bucket 6: obsolete-mechanism findings' / 'None. Zero classification records ... checked directly against the full 312-record ledger'); no candidate-unit names or per-unit rung reasoning appear anywhere in that section, contrast with Bucket 7's per-record why_each_fails detail immediately following it.
